title: Concurrency sweep and throughput lab for tokens/sec microbench
creator: Sanjay Kapoor
description:
Goal: Deliver a robust tokens-per-second microbenchmark lab that systematically measures throughput and p95 latency across concurrency, batch size, and cache-warmup profiles for our core serving models. The suite should run in CI and on nightly canaries, produce time-series results ingested into the Console dashboard, and trigger regression alerts when token/sec or p95 deviates beyond configured thresholds.

Why: Existing microbenchmarks focus on single-point steady-state runs. We need a repeatable matrix that captures concurrency scaling, contention effects, and warmup dynamics (especially KV cache and prefix caching) so we can detect regressions introduced by scheduler/kernel changes or model quantization changes.

Scope and deliverables:
- Benchmark harness that executes parametric experiments over: concurrency levels (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32), request batch sizes, sequence lengths (32, 128, 512), and warm/cold KV cache states.
- Metrics collected per run: tokens/sec (mean), token/sec (median), p50/p95/p99 latency per token and per request, CPU/GPU utilization, memory and NVMe throughput, and request fallbacks.
- Regression detection pipeline: baseline snapshots, rolling-window comparison, and automated alerts to #infra-bench when a model's p95 increases > 10% or tokens/sec drops > 8% compared to baseline for 3 consecutive runs.
- CI integration: a lightweight smoke step that runs on PRs touching runtime kernels and a scheduled nightly full sweep. Results pushed to an internal S3 bucket and annotated to PRs where regressions are detected.
- Console dashboards and historical plots per model/version/release.
- Test matrix YAML and example experiment configs in the repo.

Success criteria (acceptance):
- Harness can run a full sweep for a single model in < 3 hours on the dedicated staging pool.
- Nightly job completes with results uploaded and Dashboard shows 30-day rolling charts.
- Alerts fire for synthetic regressions injected during test phase and are routed to #infra-bench with links to failing run artifacts.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Design experiment schema (config YAML) and metrics spec (names, units, tags). 2) Implement runner that parallelizes experiment matrix while respecting isolation for cache-warm/cold runs. 3) Add metric exporters that write JSON line outputs and push aggregated summaries to S3. 4) CI job + nightly orchestrator + regression detector job. 5) Dashboard panels and alert rules. 6) Documentation + runbook.

Risks / trade-offs:
- Running full sweeps is expensive; we'll gate full sweeps to dedicated pool hours and keep PR smoke short.
- Some hardware variance across staging nodes may add noise; use per-machine baselines and noise reduction heuristics (median-of-five, trimmed mean).
- KV cache warmup behavior depends on model tokenizer and request prefixes; we'll provide standardized prompts to make warmups deterministic.

Open questions:
- Should we include quantized/INT8 variants by default or make them an opt-in label?
- How long should the baseline window be before declaring a regression? (default: 14 days)

Artifacts/links:
- Design doc: https://docs.internal.redwood.ai/confluence/throughput-observability (draft)
- Example configs: repo://infra/bench/harness/configs/sweep-template.yaml (PR coming)
- Acceptance dashboard proto: https://grafana.internal.redwood.ai/d/throughput-lab/proto
